heard: One planet in our solar system orbits completely sideways. This ice giant sits on the edge of the solar system. It takes 84 Earth years to orbit the Sun once. Most worlds spin like tops, but Uranus rolls like a ball. Its extreme tilt creates seasons that last for decades. One pole gets 42 years of nonstop daylight. The other side freezes in 42 years of pitch darkness. Voyager 2 visited in 1986 and found the coldest world. This unique orientation makes it the most lopsided world known. That frozen world still orbits completely sideways.
